newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MORE DUTCH MILLIONAIRES - BUT POORER, SURVEY SHOWS.
newsitem.headline: MORE DUTCH MILLIONAIRES - BUT POORER, SURVEY SHOWS.

text.p: In a single year the number of millionaires in the Netherlands increased by five percent to 116,000, a survey released on Thursday by Dutch statistics office CBS showed.
CBS said the number of millionaires in the Netherlands was up 5,000 year-on-year on January 1, 1995.
But although there were more millionaires they were worth less, the survey, based on tax returns and a CBS poll, showed.
Millionaires were worth an average 2.2 million guilders in 1995, 0.14 million less than a year earlier, CBS said.

It said this reflected a fall in the price of shares over the period, which shaved some 0.03 million guilders off the value of securities investments, reducing the value of the average portfolio to 0.23 million guilders.
By contrast Mr and Ms Average were slightly better off, with Dutch households booking an average 2,000 guilder increase in personal wealth to 136,000 guilders over the 12 months to January 1,1995.
The biggest single contributor to personal wealth was owner-occupied property, which accounted for around 57 percent of total household capital.
The survey also took into account entrepreneurial capital, securities holdings and bank credits, but excluded pension and life insurance entitlements and costly consumer durables and antiques.
